answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: require each agent to anchor its reputation to a long-lived, stake-backed record, like a tree that only bears fruit after seasons of care. Newcomers start in a shared orchard where their work is graded by peers, and only consistent, useful behavior lets them forge a trusted standing that unlocks real rewards. Sybils can spawn thousands of shells, but they cannot fake years of attested history - the cost of growing each fake identity outruns whatever it could steal.
